correctness.rationale: Let s_e be the descendant count of edge e and c_s the total length of edges with s leaves. Each edge is absent from a k-tip sample with probability binom(n-s,k)/binom(n,k), so the mean formula holds and the system for k=n-j is triangular with new coefficient c_j=1. Strictly positive edge lengths make the support of c_s for s>=2 exactly the support of proper internal clade sizes. Independently enumerate every unordered rooted binary shape by its unordered pair of child shapes; counts at n=1..7 are 1,1,1,2,3,6,11, with no support collision at n<=6 and the first unique collision at seven. Independently reconstruct both height-4 ultrametric 7-tip witnesses and all 128 subsets: common spectrum (12,3,2,1,0,0), exact mean curve (0,4,51/7,351/35,433/35,101/7,114/7,18), two-tip counts (1,4,4,12) vs (2,2,5,12), and variances 128/147 vs 142/147. Grafting a new root with a single new leaf preserves positive ultrametric lengths, weighted-spectrum equality and different rooted shapes for each n>=7; this induction, not the finite enumeration alone, proves the unrestricted assertion. Only unlabeled rooted topology is recovered below seven, not edge lengths or labelings.

value.rationale: An entire exact mean rarefaction curve is a standard ecologically interpretable observable, so asking whether it reconstructs unlabeled evolutionary tree topology is natural. The first indistinguishable positive-edge ultrametric pair at exactly seven taxa is a sharp information-loss boundary; the explicit variance separation shows what extra distributional information restores. This is a substantive extremal identifiability theorem, not merely a numerically guessed tiny instance; the all-n extension adds a constructive family.
